title: KEM3T controlled loopback baseline
purpose: Independent expected facts for a locally generated TCP, HTTP, and TLS fixture. This file is written before the KEM3T run and contains no observed KEM3T output.

authorization.owner: The operator running the local fixture
authorization.basis: The fixture process creates and owns every service in this dataset.
authorization.stop_condition: Stop the fixture and KEM3T process if any connection is directed outside 127.0.0.1.

entities.independent_basis: The fixture binds its listeners explicitly to the IPv4 loopback interface.
The harness starts a local HTTPServer and controls its response.
The harness starts a local TLS-wrapped HTTPServer with a newly generated self-signed certificate.
The harness binds an ephemeral loopback socket to obtain a port, then closes it before scanning. A race with another local process is possible and must be recorded if the observed state differs.

expected_observations.subject: service-http
expected_observations.adjudication: A successful TCP connect to the fixture HTTP listener confirms an open TCP endpoint.

expected_observations.subject: service-tls
expected_observations.adjudication: A successful TCP connect to the fixture TLS listener confirms an open TCP endpoint.

expected_observations.subject: port-closed
expected_observations.adjudication: Connection refusal is expected immediately after the fixture releases the port; unexpected listeners or policy behavior must be recorded as a fixture deviation.

expected_observations.subject: service-http
expected_observations.adjudication: The response is generated by the harness handler. The title and header are fixture identifiers, not proof of a real software product.

expected_observations.subject: service-tls
expected_observations.adjudication: The certificate is generated locally for this run. KEM3T may extract metadata and a fingerprint, but must not label this certificate trusted.

prohibited_inferences: An open TCP port alone proves a vulnerability.
The fixture HTTP title or response header proves a particular production software identity.
The self-signed fixture certificate proves malicious activity.
The loopback fixture provides evidence about public DNS, ownership, ASN, CDN, or third-party infrastructure.
known_unknowns: Certificate Transparency and public RDAP results
Passive DNS and external threat-intelligence coverage
Cross-host relationships and multi-hop path validity
Behavior under packet filtering or non-loopback network conditions
